item.title: data.table vs dplyr vs tidytable in 2026: Which R Data Library Should You Actually Use?
item.description: An R script that reads a 4 GB CSV, groups by three columns and writes a summary should not take longer than your coffee break — but the same job can run in seconds or in minutes depending on which data library you load. That difference is not academic. It decides whether an analyst iterates five times an hour or twice a day, and it decides whether a laptop with 16 GB of RAM can hold the working set at all.

item.title: Self-Hosted DataFrame Processing Libraries: Polars vs Vaex vs datatable
item.description:
Introduction

When building self-hosted data pipelines, choosing the right DataFrame library can dramatically impact performance, memory usage, and developer productivity. While pandas remains the de facto standard for in-memory data manipulation, three open-source alternatives — Polars, Vaex, and datatable — offer significant advantages for server-side workloads: lazy evaluation, out-of-core processing, and multi-threaded execution.
